The change follows the existing pattern. RestService (src/angular/src/app/services/utils/rest.service.ts) is the app's single HTTP wrapper. sendRequest, post and delete all share the same map(handleSuccess) / catchError(handleError) / shareReplay(1) pipeline. Adding an optional `body` to post() extends that wrapper and does not create a second path. No new dependency, no import cycle, and no reach into another module's internals.

The change is backward compatible. `body ?? null` keeps the exact wire behavior for the 4 existing no-body callers: model-file.service.ts:61, :74 and :87, and server-command.service.ts:26. They still send a null POST body. Angular HttpClient serializes a plain object as JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json automatically, which matches the backend's move to bottle.request.json in phase 111-01.

Existing deviation, not introduced by this diff: src/angular/src/app/services/server/bulk-command.service.ts:118 calls HttpClient.post directly with a JSON body and does its own error-message extraction, bypassing RestService. That made sense while RestService.post could not send a body. This change removes that reason. Moving BulkCommandService onto RestService is not a clean swap: it parses typed JSON responses and reads err.error.error, while RestService returns text. Treat it as a possible future consolidation, not a defect. Today there is only one bypass site, which is below the rule-of-three threshold.

Asymmetry for the next step (config.service.ts migration): src/angular/src/app/tests/mocks/mock-rest.service.ts only defines sendRequest(_url) (line 6). It has no post(). Once config.service.ts switches to post(url, body), any spec that injects MockRestService will need the mock extended. pending: whoever does the config.service.ts migration should confirm this. It is a test-sufficiency/impact concern for that later change, not a finding against this diff.

Minor API-shape note: the `body?: object` type is broad, so primitives can't be passed (good), but any object can. That matches how loosely typed the rest of RestService is (string URLs, text responses), so it is consistent and not a finding.
No intent-context block was provided, so intent_doc_match was not attempted. Git history (phase 111, config-set GET->POST migration) suggests this is the planned frontend groundwork for that change.
